title: Babylon becomes an imperial capital
summary: Babylon served as the capital of the Neo-Babylonian Empire between 626 and 539 BCE. Walls, gates, palaces and temples preserve traces of a city with a much longer history.

claims.text: Babylon served as the capital of the Neo-Babylonian Empire between 626 and 539 BCE. Walls, gates, palaces and temples preserve traces of a city with a much longer history.
Conventional imperial phase, not the foundation and abandonment of Babylon.
A capital’s imperial phase is not the lifespan of its population or culture. This band can be compared with other states while keeping earlier and later Babylonian histories outside its stated scope.
